verses.text: "Isn't human life on earth a term of hard labor? Aren't our days like those of a hired worker?
Like a servant desperate for shade, like a hired worker waiting for his pay,
I've been given months of misery and assigned nights of weariness.
When I lie down, I ask, 'When can I get up? When will this night end?' I toss and turn until dawn.
My body is covered with worms and clumps of dirt. My skin closes up and then breaks open again.
My days pass faster than a weaver's shuttle and run out without hope.
Remember that my life is just a breath. My eyes won't see good days again.
Those who see me now will see me no more. You'll look for me, but I'll be gone.
As a cloud fades and disappears, so anyone who goes down to Sheol never comes back up.
They'll never return to their home, and the place they belonged to won't know them anymore.
So I won't keep quiet. I'll speak from the anguish in my spirit and complain out of the bitterness of my soul.
Am I the sea or a sea monster that you have to put a guard over me?
When I say, 'My bed will comfort me, and my couch will give me some relief,'
you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
I'd rather be strangled and die than live in this body.
I hate my life. I don't want to live forever. Leave me alone, because my days are only a breath.
What are human beings that you make so much of them and pay them so much attention,
checking on them every morning and testing them at every moment?
Won't you look away long enough to let me swallow my own spit?
If I've sinned, what have I done to you, watcher of human beings? Why have you made me your target, so I've become a burden to myself?
Why don't you forgive my disobedience and take away my guilt? Soon I'll lie down in the dust. You'll search for me, but I'll be gone."
